st.2: It was excavated by Rafique Mughal from 1974.
st.3: Its Period I goes back to about 4000 BCE.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Mehrgarh was excavated by J.-F. Jarrige, not Rafique Mughal; its Period I goes back to about 7000 BCE, not 4000 BCE; and it is a Neolithic, pre-Harappan site, not a Mature Harappan city.

st.1: Rhinoceros remains have been found at Amri, in Punjab.
st.2: Kot Diji, in Baluchistan, was a fortified settlement destroyed by fire.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Amri is in Sindh, not Punjab; Kot Diji is also in Sindh, not Baluchistan; and the Hakra culture belongs to the Ghaggar-Hakra (Cholistan) area, not Gujarat.

st.4: The water buffalo, rather than the humped bull, was the favoured domestic animal.
st.3: Camel bones have been found only at Lothal.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Horse remains are not well established in the early and mature levels; camel bones come from Kalibangan, so they are not confined to Lothal; and the humped bull (zebu), not the water buffalo, was the favoured domestic animal.

st.3: Lahuradeva in Bihar has the oldest paddy according to the latest research.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Mahagara is known for its cattle pen and early rice, not barley; and Lahuradeva, which has the oldest paddy, is in Uttar Pradesh, not Bihar.

st.2: The Periplus names Muziris as the only port on the east coast.
st.1: The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea (c. 60 CE) was written by Ptolemy.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Periplus was written by an anonymous Greek sailor, not Ptolemy; the only east-coast port it names is Koddura, Muziris being on the west coast; and Megasthenes credits the Andhras with an infantry of 1,00,000, not 3,00,000.

st.2: It derives the Brahmana from the mouth and the Rajanya (Kshatriya) from the arms of the Purusha.

x: All three statements are correct: the Purusha Sukta (Rigveda X.90) is a late addition in the 10th Mandala; it derives the Brahmana from the mouth and the Rajanya from the arms (the Vaishya from the thighs and the Shudra from the feet); and the word Shudra first appears in it, not in the family books.

st.3: Chudakarma (tonsure) marked the child's initiation into Vedic study.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The Acharya taught the Veda without charging a fee, while the Upadhyaya taught for a livelihood; and initiation into Vedic study was the Upanayana, Chudakarma being the tonsure of the child's third year.

st.2: Rock Edict XIII gave condemned prisoners a respite of three days.
st.1: Ashoka freed prisoners on each anniversary of his birth.

x: Neither statement is correct. Ashoka freed prisoners on the anniversaries of his coronation (Abhisheka), not his birth; and the three-day respite for condemned prisoners was given by Pillar Edict IV, not Rock Edict XIII.

st.3: The seven caves of the two hills are together called the Saptaparni caves.
st.1: The Lomas Rishi and Sudama caves are on the Nagarjuni hill.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Lomas Rishi and Sudama are on the Barabar hill, not Nagarjuni; Gopika is the largest cave of the Nagarjuni group, not Barabar; and the seven caves are together called Satghar, the Saptaparni cave being the council cave at Rajgir.

st.3: The Mauryan state did not enforce a single official faith but patronised several sects.

x: All three statements are correct: Chandragupta followed Bhadrabahu to Shravanabelagola; Pillar Edict VII names the Ajivikas and the Nirgranthas separately; and the Mauryan state patronised several sects instead of enforcing one official faith.

st.3: Ghatotkacha
st.2: Skandagupta

x: Kaviraja was the title of Samudragupta, Mahendraditya of Kumaragupta I and Sakari of Chandragupta II; Chandragupta I was the first Gupta to assume the title Maharajadhiraja (Ghatotkacha was only a Maharaja, and Skandagupta held none of these titles).

st.3: They did not mint coins, minting being a royal prerogative.

x: All three statements are correct: Chola village assemblies were the proprietors of village lands, they could raise loans, and they did not mint coins, which remained a royal prerogative.

st.4: He relied mainly on the levies of iqta-holders rather than a large standing army.
st.3: After 1306 the Beas became the boundary between the Sultanate and the Mongols.

st.1: Nobles opposed to him plotted to enthrone his brother Daulat Khan.
st.4: Krishnadevaraya and Mahmud Gawan were his contemporaries.
st.3: He was defeated by Rana Sanga at Khanua.

x: None of the statements is correct. The nobles plotted to enthrone his brother Jalal Khan (Daulat Khan Lodi was the governor of the Punjab); Ibrahim seized Gwalior, not Ranthambhor, for sheltering Jalal Khan; Rana Sanga defeated him at Khatoli, Khanua (1527) being Babur's victory over Sanga; and his contemporaries were Krishnadevaraya and Sultan Quli, not Mahmud Gawan, who died in 1481.

st.3: The Mir Bakhshi dealt with religion, charity and madad-i-maash grants.
st.1: Jahangir made the post of Wakil largely symbolic.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. It was Akbar, not Jahangir, who made the Wakil's post symbolic; religion, charity and madad-i-maash grants were under the Sadr-us-Sudur, not the Mir Bakhshi; and the Qazi-ul-Quzat was the chief justice, the military department being under the Mir Bakhshi.

st.1: Even watan jagirs were transferred every 3-4 years so that their holders did not strike local roots.
st.2: 'Tankhwah' meant mansabdars kept waiting without jagirs.
st.4: J.F. Richards linked the crisis to the influx of Deccani and Maratha nobles.

Richards'.

x: All three statements are correct: the Sayyid brothers were king-makers from 1713 to 1720, Husain Ali Khan was killed in 1720, and Saadat Khan joined Muhammad Shah against them.

st.2: He was the first Mughal emperor to become a pensioner of the French East India Company.
st.1: He was blinded by Najib-ud-Daula Rohilla in 1788.
st.3: The English captured Delhi in 1818 during his reign.

st.1: Malhar Rao Holkar was the overall Maratha commander, with the Peshwa's son Vishwas Rao as nominal head; both were killed.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The overall Maratha commander was Sadashiv Rao Bhau, not Malhar Rao Holkar (who survived the battle); and Abdali's allies were Najib-ud-Daula and Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh, Suraj Mal of Bharatpur having kept away.

st.3: The Danes set up their first factory at Serampore in 1620 and made Tranquebar their headquarters in 1755.
st.4: The Danes sold Serampore and Tranquebar to the French in 1845.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Yanam lies in the Godavari delta, not the Krishna delta; the Danes' first factory was at Tranquebar (1620) and Serampore became their headquarters (1755), not the reverse; and they sold their settlements to the British, not the French, in 1845.

st.3: Ordinances issued by the Viceroy were valid for six months.

x: All three statements are correct: the Indian Councils Act, 1861 reflected the lesson of 1857 that Indians should be associated with law-making; at least half of the additional members were non-official; and the Viceroy's ordinances were valid for six months.

st.4: Under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle Pondicherry was returned to the French in exchange for Louisburg.
st.1: The First Carnatic War was linked to the War of the Spanish Succession.
st.3: The Third Carnatic War was an extension of the Seven Years' War and ended with the Treaty of Pondicherry (1763).

The First Carnatic War was linked to the Austrian War of Succession, not the Spanish; the Second was fought from 1749 to 1754, not 1750 to 1755; the Third ended with the Treaty of Paris (1763), the Treaty of Pondicherry having closed the Second; and at Aix-la-Chapelle it was Madras that was returned to the English in exchange for Louisburg (the English had failed to take Pondicherry).

st.1: The Vartamana Vyavaharikandhra Bhasha Parivartaka Samajam was founded by Veeresalingam, with Gidugu Ramamurthy as its secretary.

x: All three statements are correct: the Samajam was founded by Veeresalingam (president) with Gidugu Ramamurthy as secretary; the Vyavaharika Bhashodyama Samstha was formed in 1910 after the Visakhapatnam meeting; and in the 1913 Madras University controversy the majority kept the literary dialect.

st.1: Krishna Patrika (1902) of Machilipatnam was founded by Konda Venkatappayya, its first editor, and was later edited by Mutnuri Krishna Rao.

x: All three statements are correct: Krishna Patrika was founded by Konda Venkatappayya, its first editor, and later edited by Mutnuri Krishna Rao; Andhra Geeta Svarajya was started by T. Prakasam at Madras in 1921; and Nilagiri Patrika (1922) of Nalgonda was the first Telugu paper in Telangana.

st.1: Rajahmundry, with Venkataratnam Naidu's Brahma Mandir, was a centre of the Brahmo movement in Andhra.
st.2: K. Seethamma organised the women's wing of the Arya Samaj.

x: None of the statements is correct. Venkataratnam Naidu's Brahma Mandir was at Kakinada, not Rajahmundry; K. Seethamma organised the women's wing of the Prarthana Samaj, not the Arya Samaj; and Sridharalu Naidu translated Brahmo books into Tamil and Telugu, not Kannada.

st.1: Madan Mohan Malaviya founded the Central Hindu College at Benaras in 1898.
st.2: The Banaras Hindu University was founded in 1920 by Madan Mohan Malaviya with Besant.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The Central Hindu College (1898) was founded by Annie Besant, not Malaviya; BHU was founded in 1916, not 1920; and its foundation stone was laid by Viceroy Lord Hardinge II, not Malaviya.

st.3: It was later shifted to Aligarh.

x: All three statements are correct: the Scientific Society was founded by Sayyid Ahmad Khan at Ghazipur in 1864, it translated Western works into Urdu, and it was later shifted to Aligarh.

st.2: Missions of the Berlin Committee went only to Turkey and Kabul, not to Persia.
st.4: The Afghan Amir Habibullah openly helped the Provisional Government.
st.1: The Berlin Committee sought the help of Russia and Japan to free India.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Berlin Committee sought the help of Germany and Turkey, not Russia and Japan; its missions went to Baghdad, Persia, Turkey and Kabul; the Provisional Government at Kabul was set up in December 1915, not 1917; and it was crown prince Amanullah who helped it, Amir Habibullah having stayed neutral.

st.1: She came to India in 1893 and became President of the Theosophical Society in 1917.
st.4: Her protégé Jiddu Krishnamurti wrote 'The Secret Doctrine'.
st.3: The first principal of her National College, Madanapalle (1916), was C.W. Leadbeater.

x: None of the statements is correct. Besant became President of the Theosophical Society in 1907 (1917 was her INC presidency); BHU was founded by Madan Mohan Malaviya in 1916, her Central Hindu College being its nucleus; the first principal at Madanapalle was J.H. Cousins, not Leadbeater; and 'The Secret Doctrine' is Blavatsky's, Krishnamurti having written 'At the Feet of the Master'.

st.2: Lala Lajpat Rai, who led the Lahore protest, had presided over the first session of the AITUC in 1920.

x: All three statements are correct: Nehru and G.B. Pant were beaten at Lucknow; Lala Lajpat Rai had presided over the first AITUC session in 1920; and black flags were shown at Guntur and Ongole.

st.3: Gandhi pleaded guilty, was sentenced to six years and was released in 1926 on health grounds.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Gandhi was charged under Section 124A for articles in Young India, not Navajivan; and he was released in 1924 on health grounds, not 1926.

st.3: A mass civil disobedience struggle under Gandhi's leadership

x: All three were part of the Quit India Resolution: an immediate end of British rule, a provisional government after the British withdrawal, and a non-violent mass struggle under Gandhi.

st.3: He gave priority to village and cottage industries over heavy industry.

x: All three statements are correct: Gandhi was not against modern industry as such and was close to G.D. Birla; he linked trusteeship to South Africa, 1903; and he gave priority to village and cottage industries over heavy industry.

st.2: 'Feathers and Stones', his prison diary, was written by him.

x: All three statements are correct: Pattabhi Sitaramayya wrote the 'History of the Indian National Congress' and the prison diary 'Feathers and Stones', and founded the Andhra Bank at Machilipatnam in 1923.

st.1: Gandhi took the word 'Harijan' from the Gujarati saint Narsinh Mehta.

x: All three statements are correct: Gandhi took 'Harijan' from Narsinh Mehta; the Vijayawada branch was headed by Kasinathuni Nageswara Rao; and the Sangh was founded in 1932 as the All India Anti-Untouchability League.

st.2: The Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act was enacted in 1956.

x: All three statements are correct: the Hindu Marriage Act dates from 1955, the Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act from 1956, and Article 30 protects minority educational institutions.

st.2: On 3 March 2022 the AP High Court ruled against the three-capitals plan and directed that Amaravati be developed.

x: All three statements are correct: Amaravati was chosen in 2015 with about 33,000 acres pooled; on 3 March 2022 the High Court ruled against the three-capitals plan; and the 2026 Amendment Act made Amaravati the sole capital with effect from 2 June 2024.

st.3: Dolmens were the burials of elites, while commoners were buried in pits.

x: All three statements are correct: the megaliths are popularly called 'Rakshasa Gullu', they belong to the Iron Age, and dolmens were elite burials while commoners were buried in pits.

st.4: Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription calls Gautamiputra Satakarni 'Agama-nilaya'.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Chhandogya Upanishad names Ghora Angirasa, not Yajnavalkya, as Krishna's teacher; and it is the Nasik inscription, not Rudradaman's Junagadh inscription, that calls Gautamiputra Satakarni 'Agama-nilaya'.

st.3: Prakrit, the people's language, helped Buddhism become a mass movement.

x: All three statements are correct: guilds held deposits and paid the interest to the monks, Yavana merchants funded caves in the western Deccan, and Prakrit, the people's language, helped Buddhism become a mass movement.

st.2: Lokamahadevi, queen of Vikramaditya II, built the Virupaksha temple at Aihole.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Lokamahadevi's Virupaksha temple is at Pattadakal, not Aihole; and Kirtivarman II was overthrown by the Rashtrakuta Dantidurga, not Dhruva.

st.2: The first Telugu word, Nagabu, was found at Bhattiprolu by Veturi Prabhakara Sastri.
st.1: Hala's Gathasaptasati, in Sanskrit, contains Telugu words such as atta, potta, pilla and pandi.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The Gathasaptasati is in Prakrit (Maharashtri), not Sanskrit; Nagabu was found at Amaravati, not Bhattiprolu; and Vepuru occurs in the Myakadoni inscription, not the Chikkulla plates.

st.1: It followed strict classical metrical rules.

x: All three statements are correct: the prabandha kept to strict classical metres; in the Reddi courts it was supported by Errana and Srinatha; and it reached its peak with the Ashtadiggajas.

st.1: Krishnadevaraya fought the sieges of Kondavidu and Kondapalli (1515–16) against the Qutb Shahis of Golconda.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. The Kondavidu and Kondapalli sieges were against the Gajapatis, not the Qutb Shahis; and at Raichur (1520) Krishnadevaraya defeated the Adil Shah of Bijapur, not the Qutb Shah.

st.2: He married Narama and Perama, daughters of Pinnachodi, and made their brother Jayapa Gajasahani.

x: All three statements are correct: Mutyalachaundaraya took Divi in the 1201 campaign; Ganapatideva married Narama and Perama, daughters of Pinnachodi, and made their brother Jayapa Gajasahani; and in 1257 he killed Mummadi Rajendra Chola with Akkana and Bayyana.

st.2: He merged the eight tarafs into four provinces.
st.1: He was a Persian (Afaqi) noble and wazir of Firuz Shah Bahmani.

x: None of the statements is correct. Mahmud Gawan was wazir of Muhammad Shah III, not Firuz Shah; he divided the four tarafs into eight provinces, not the reverse; and he crushed the Telangana revolts with Velama, not Reddi, help.

st.1: He was the Abyssinian regent of the Adil Shahis and fought Jahangir.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Malik Ambar was regent of the Nizam Shahis of Ahmednagar, not the Adil Shahis; and his revenue system on Todar Mal's lines avoided revenue farming.

st.2: The new city of Vijayanagara was completed c. 1343, under Harihara II's oversight.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The new city was completed c. 1343 under Bukka I's oversight, not Harihara II's; and the royal emblem was the Varaha (boar), not the Garuda.

st.2: The Devarakonda fort is a 14th-century hill fort of the Recherla Velamas.

x: All three statements are correct: the Rachakonda fort is of cyclopean masonry without mortar, Devarakonda is a 14th-century Velama hill fort, and Sultan Quli Qutb Shah annexed both.

st.2: Anavota Reddi defeated Madanayudu and his nephew Naganayudu at Dharanikota, foiling their bid to avenge Singama.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. At Dharanikota Madanayudu and Naganayudu defeated Anavota Reddi and avenged Singama; and the titles the Velamas took were Jagadabbaganda and Rayavesa Bhujanga, Andhra Suratrana being Kapaya Nayaka's title.

st.1: It lies in Kurnool district.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Tadipatri lies in Anantapur district, not Kurnool; and its Chintala Venkataramana temple is dedicated to Vishnu and the Bugga Ramalingeswara temple to Shiva, not the reverse.

st.1: It is popularly known as the Hazara Rama temple.
st.2: It was begun under Krishnadevaraya, expanded by Achyutaraya and completed under Devaraya II.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The Vitthala temple is the Saptaswara Devalayam, the Hazara Rama being a separate temple; it was begun under Devaraya II, expanded by Krishnadevaraya and continued under Achyutaraya; and it has 56 musical pillars, not 108.

st.2: Turrebaz Khan was later shot near Aurangabad.

st.4: For its loyalty, Hyderabad got back Berar, and Afzal-ud-Daula received the Star of India.

x: None of the statements is correct. The attack was repulsed by Resident Col. Davidson, not James Kirkpatrick; Turrebaz Khan was shot near Toopran, not Aurangabad; Maulvi Allauddin was transported and died in the Andamans (1884), not hanged; and Hyderabad got back the Raichur Doab and Dharashiv, not Berar.

st.2: It was led by Unnava Lakshminarayana.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The Palnadu forest satyagraha was led by Kanneganti Hanumanthu (Unnava Lakshminarayana only backed it); and it took place in Palnadu, Guntur district, not Nellore.

st.1: It was dedicated to Kompella Janardhana Rao.

x: All three statements are correct: Mahaprasthanam was dedicated to Kompella Janardhana Rao, its poems were written between 1933 and 1947 beginning with Jayabheri, and it was published in 1950.

st.1: He was invited to Andhra by Tanguturi Prakasam.
st.2: He delivered five lectures at Machilipatnam.

x: Neither statement is correct. Bipin Chandra Pal was invited by Mutnuri Krishna Rao, not T. Prakasam; and his five lectures were delivered at Rajahmundry, not Machilipatnam.

st.4: Tapeswaram Kaja received its GI tag in 2017.
st.3: Budithi bell and brass craft, of Vizianagaram district, received its GI tag in 2008.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Bandar Laddu got its GI tag in 2017, not 2011; Budithi is in Srikakulam district, not Vizianagaram; and Tapeswaram Kaja has no GI tag.

st.4: Art Lovers, founded by B. Narsinga Rao and Gaddar, was renamed Praja Natya Mandali in 1971.
st.3: Its first meeting was at Warangal and its first poetry collection was Jhamjha.

st.2: Sir Alladi Krishnaswami Ayyar
st.4: H.C. Mukherjee and T.T. Krishnamachari

st.2: The Puranas call Chandragupta Maurya 'Sarvakshatrantaka'.
st.1: The Haryanka dynasty immediately preceded the Nandas in Magadha.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The Shishunagas, not the Haryankas, immediately preceded the Nandas; the Puranas call Mahapadma Nanda, not Chandragupta Maurya, 'Sarvakshatrantaka'; and Mahapadma founded the Nanda dynasty, the Haryanka line being Bimbisara's.

st.2: The amphorae found at Arikamedu and Kodumanal were jars used mainly for wine and oil.

x: All three statements are correct: Wheeler excavated Arikamedu in 1945, the amphorae were double-handled jars for wine and oil, and Muziris has been identified with Pattanam in Ernakulam district.

st.2: He was defeated by the Pallava Simhavarman, as the Manchikallu inscription shows.

x: All three statements are correct: Rudrapurushadatta, the last Ikshvaku, was defeated by the Pallava Simhavarman (Manchikallu inscription), and the victory helped establish Pallava rule in the Krishna valley.

st.3: The Andhra-origin theory rests on early Prakrit charters from the Krishna–Guntur region and their replacement of the Vishnukundins.
st.1: Their capital was Mamallapuram.
st.4: They were originally feudatories of the Badami Chalukyas.

x: None of the statements is correct. st.2: Rajaraja I granted the village of Anaimangalam to the Chudamani Vihara at Kanchipuram.
st.1: Temple income came only from royal grants, never from guild donations.

st.1: The First Battle of Tarain arose over Ghori's attack on Ajmer.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The First Battle arose over Ghori's attack on Tabarhinda (Bhatinda), not Ajmer; and Jaichand of Kannauj sent no troops to help Prithviraj in the Second Battle.

st.2: India is presently described as being in the ageing stage, past its youth bulge.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. India is presently in the youth-bulge stage, not the ageing stage; and its demographic dividend window is expected to last till about 2055, not 2035.

st.2: A.M. Shah wrote The Household Dimension of the Family in India in 1973.

x: All three statements are correct: K.M. Kapadia pioneered family studies, A.M. Shah wrote The Household Dimension of the Family in India in 1973, and for Irawati Karve jointness rests on functional unity and obligations.

st.1: The Chenchus, settled agriculturists, live in the Nallamala forests of Kurnool, Prakasam and Guntur.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The Chenchus are hunters and food-gatherers, not settled agriculturists; and the Savara and Jatapu live mainly in Srikakulam and Vizianagaram, not the Godavari districts.

st.3: Bombay State was split into Maharashtra and Gujarat in 1966.
st.4: The Inner Line Permit system dates from 1950.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The States Reorganisation Commission was headed by Fazl Ali, K.M. Panikkar being a member; Bombay was split in 1960, not 1966; and the Inner Line Permit system dates from 1873, not 1950.

st.1: The Sara Nishedha Udyamam (1991-92) was started by rural women of Dubagunta in Nellore district.

x: All three statements are correct: the anti-arrack movement began with the women of Dubagunta in Nellore district; 'Visakha Ukku – Andhrula Hakku' is linked with T. Amrutha Rao's fast; and the Srikakulam girijan movement turned Naxalite.

st.4: Termination ends the cycle, with no feedback into agenda setting.

st.1: Social welfare consists of universal services for the whole population rather than for particular groups.
st.2: Social security refers to rehabilitation in deviant or vulnerable situations such as drugs, beggary and juvenile delinquency.

st.2: Summative evaluation judges a programme at its end, on the basis of outcomes.

x: All three statements are correct: monitoring watches the main components while a programme runs; summative evaluation judges it at the end on outcomes; and communication and transparency run through every stage.

st.1: India's official poverty line is based on consumption expenditure.

x: All three statements are correct: India's poverty line is based on consumption expenditure, size of the house is not a social indicator of poverty, and Oscar Lewis propounded the 'culture of poverty' in 1959.

st.4: Bihar's Mukhyamantri Vriddhajan Pension Yojana is limited to BPL households.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The minimum age for ST beneficiaries in AP is 50 years, not 55; and Bihar's scheme is universal, with no income or BPL bar.

st.3: The 2019 Amendment Bill removing the cap has not been enacted.

x: All three statements are correct: the Maintenance Tribunal works at sub-division level, the maximum maintenance is Rs 10,000 a month, and the 2019 Amendment Bill has not been enacted.

st.3: Its phase 1 covered 12 lakh families.
st.4: It aims to end extreme poverty by 2047.

st.3: It amended the IPC and CrPC.

x: All three statements are correct: the AP Disha Bill proposed investigation in 7 days and trial in 14 days, and it amended the IPC and CrPC.

st.1: It was enacted as the Untouchability (Offences) Act and came into force on 19 November 1976.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. The Untouchability (Offences) Act came into force on 1 June 1955 (19 November 1976 is when the renaming took effect); and 30 January 1990 is the commencement of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, not this Act.

st.4: Pakistan closed the corridor in May 2025 after Operation Sindoor.
st.1: It is a 4.7-km visa-free corridor from Dera Baba Nanak (Gurdaspur) to Gurdwara Panja Sahib (Hasan Abdal).

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The corridor runs to Gurdwara Darbar Sahib, Kartarpur (Narowal), not Panja Sahib; the agreement was renewed for 5 years, not 10, in October 2024; and it was India, not Pakistan, that closed the corridor in May 2025.

st.3: Lal Bahadur Shastri visited Kabul in September 1959.
st.2: Operation Pawan (1984–86) was the IPKF deployment in Sri Lanka.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Operation Cactus (1988) foiled a coup in the Maldives, not Sri Lanka; Operation Pawan, the IPKF deployment, ran from 1987 to 1990, not 1984 to 1986; and it was Jawaharlal Nehru, not Shastri, who visited Kabul in September 1959.

st.3: The 'India Out' campaign is associated with the Maldives' domestic politics.

x: All three statements are correct: Favara was linked with UPI in August 2026, the Greater Male Connectivity project is a bridge-causeway, and 'India Out' was a Maldivian campaign.

st.2: India has ratified C87 and C98.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. India has not ratified C87 and C98 (freedom of association and collective bargaining), though it has ratified C100 and C111; and it has not ratified C189 on Domestic Workers.

st.3: In 2011 BRICS had about 11% of world GDP but about 20% of IMF votes.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Expanded BRICS accounts for about half of the world's population, not a quarter; and in 2011 BRICS had about 20% of world GDP but only about 11% of IMF votes, not the reverse.

st.2: Its Review Conferences are held every five years.

x: All three statements are correct: the NPT was signed in 1968, came into force in 1970 and was extended indefinitely in 1995; its Review Conferences are held every five years; and it recognises as NWS those that tested before 1 January 1967.

st.4: The US strikes on Iran in July 2026 damaged the Chabahar terminal.
st.2: India develops its Shahid Beheshti terminal through the Shipping Corporation of India (SCI).
st.1: It lies in Sistan-Baluchestan province of Iran on the Persian Gulf.

x: None of the statements is correct. Chabahar is on the Gulf of Oman, outside the Persian Gulf; India develops the Shahid Beheshti terminal through IPGL, not the Shipping Corporation of India; the 10-year contract was signed in May 2024, not 2022; and the July 2026 US strikes did not damage the terminal.

st.3: Diego Garcia, a US-UK base, was the subject of a treaty between the UK and Seychelles in May 2025.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. China's first overseas military base (2017) is at Djibouti, not Gwadar; and the May 2025 treaty on Diego Garcia was between the UK and Mauritius, not Seychelles.

st.3: Samudrayaan and Matsya-6000 are part of ISRO's Gaganyaan programme.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Samudrayaan and Matsya-6000 belong to the Deep Ocean Mission, not ISRO's Gaganyaan programme; and India's latest coastline estimate is 11,098.81 km, not 7,516.6 km.

st.3: Each State has a separate constitution of its own.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. A rigid constitution is a federal feature, not a unitary one; and the States have no separate constitutions of their own, a single constitution being a unitary feature.

st.1: Montesquieu, in 'The Spirit of Laws' (1748), drew mainly on the British Constitution for his theory of separation of powers.

x: All three statements are correct: Montesquieu drew mainly on the British Constitution; Ambedkar preferred the parliamentary system for giving priority to responsibility over stability; and in India the President is the nominal head and the Council of Ministers the real executive.

st.4: Article 141 lets the Supreme Court do complete justice and fill gaps in the law.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Articles 122 and 212 bar courts from questioning legislative proceedings on the ground of irregular procedure; and the power to do complete justice is in Article 142, not Article 141.

st.3: Of 2,473 amendments proposed, 7,635 were discussed.
st.2: The Draft Constitution was considered for 2 years, 11 months and 18 days.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The Draft Constitution was considered for 114 days (2 years, 11 months and 18 days was the Assembly's whole span); of 7,635 amendments proposed, 2,473 were discussed, not the reverse; and 284 members, not all 299, signed the Constitution on 24 January 1950.

st.3: Maithili was added by the 92nd Amendment in 2003.

x: All three statements are correct: the Eighth Schedule originally had 14 languages, Sindhi was added by the 21st Amendment (1967) and Maithili by the 92nd Amendment (2003).

st.2: Article 7 provides that a person who voluntarily acquires the citizenship of a foreign State is not a citizen of India.
st.1: Under Article 6, a person domiciled in India who had been ordinarily resident in India for 5 years before the commencement became a citizen.
st.3: Article 10 provides for the continuance of the rights of citizenship, subject to the President's order.

x: None of the statements is correct. Domicile with 5 years' ordinary residence is Article 5, not Article 6; loss of citizenship on voluntarily acquiring a foreign one is Article 9, not Article 7; Article 10 makes continuance subject to Parliament's law, not the President's order; and the power to regulate acquisition and termination of citizenship is in Article 11, not Article 10.

st.2: Article 25 protects the individual's freedom of religion, while Article 26 protects the collective freedom of religious denominations.

x: All three statements are correct: Articles 27 and 28(1) are State-neutrality provisions; Article 25 protects individual and Article 26 collective religious freedom; and in May 2026 the Court left the Article 26(a) question to the Ministry of Education.

st.2: A proclamation of Financial Emergency must be approved by a special majority in each House of Parliament.

x: Neither statement is correct. Proclamations of both President's Rule and Financial Emergency are approved by a simple majority in each House; only a National Emergency needs a special majority.

st.4: Amaravati became the sole capital of Andhra Pradesh from 2 June 2014.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. The Court directed J&K Assembly elections by 30 September 2024, not 31 December 2024; and Amaravati became the sole capital with effect from 2 June 2024, not 2014.

st.2: Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 amend the First and Seventh Schedules.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Laws under Articles 2 and 3 amend the First and Fourth Schedules, not the Seventh; and under Article 4 they are not deemed amendments of the Constitution for Article 368.

st.4: If both offices are vacant, the Speaker of the Lok Sabha discharges the President's functions under the President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969.
st.2: While acting as President, he continues to draw the salary of the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. While acting as President, the Vice-President does not preside over the Rajya Sabha and draws the President's emoluments, not the Chairman's salary; and if both offices are vacant, the Chief Justice of India, not the Speaker, discharges the President's functions.

st.1: Under Article 86(1), not more than six months may pass between the last sitting of one session and the first sitting of the next.
st.4: Joint sittings of the two Houses have been held only twice.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The six-month rule is in Article 85(1), not Article 86(1); the Constitution prescribes no minimum number of sitting days; and joint sittings have been held three times (1961, 1978, 2002), not twice.

st.3: The criticism of the collegium as 'imperium in imperio' refers to its domination by the executive.
st.2: The appointment of a High Court Chief Justice begins with a proposal from the State's Chief Minister.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The appointment of a High Court Chief Justice begins with the recommendation of the CJI and the two senior-most Supreme Court judges, not the Chief Minister; 'imperium in imperio' criticises the collegium as a self-contained authority within the State, not as executive-dominated; and P.S. Narasimha joined the collegium when J.K. Maheshwari, not B.V. Nagarathna, retired in June 2026.

st.2: About 12.4% of the pending cases were in the High Courts.

x: All three statements are correct: in May 2022 over 4.7 crore cases were pending, 87.4% in subordinate courts (over 4 crore) and about 12.4% in the High Courts.

st.2: A Joint Administrative Tribunal cannot serve more than one State.
st.4: The AP Administrative Tribunal was constituted by an order of the Governor of 19 May 1975 under Article 371D(3).

x: Only statement 3 is correct. A State Administrative Tribunal is set up by the Central Government at the State's request, not by the State under its own law; a Joint Administrative Tribunal can serve two or more States; and APAT was constituted by a Presidential order, not the Governor's, under Article 371D(3).

st.1: They are appointed by the Governor of the State to whose cadre they belong.

x: Neither statement is correct. All India Services officers are appointed by the President, not the Governor; and they can be dismissed only by the Central Government, not by the State Government under which they serve.

st.2: It functions under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.

x: All three statements are correct: the NCSK was constituted in 1994 under the 1993 Act and became non-statutory after 2004; it works under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment; and its tenure has been extended to 31 March 2028.

st.1: A Minorities Commission was first set up by a resolution of the Ministry of Minority Affairs in 1978 and was made statutory by the NCM Act, 1992.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The 1978 Minorities Commission was set up by a resolution of the Ministry of Home Affairs (the Ministry of Minority Affairs came only in 2006); and Jains were notified as a national minority in 2014, not 2004.

st.1: It was decided by the Supreme Court in 2003.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Vineet Narain was decided in 1997, not 2003; and it struck down, not upheld, the 'Single Directive'.

st.1: Bihar and Uttar Pradesh have only a Lokayukta, without an Upa-Lokayukta.

x: All three statements are correct: Bihar and UP have only a Lokayukta; by 2013, 21 States and one UT had Lokayuktas; and Section 63 of the 2013 Act requires every State to set up a Lokayukta within one year.

st.1: It was set up in 1990 under Article 262.
st.3: Its 11th and last meeting was held on 16 July 2006.

x: None of the statements is correct. The Inter-State Council was set up in 1990 under Article 263, not Article 262 (water disputes); it is chaired by the Prime Minister, not the Home Minister; and its 11th and last meeting was held on 16 July 2016, not 2006.

st.1: The National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution, set up in February 2000 under R.S. Sarkaria, reported in 2002.
st.2: The Second Administrative Reforms Commission was constituted in 2005, and Veerappa Moily succeeded V. Ramachandran as its chairman in 2009.

x: None of the statements is correct. The NCRWC was chaired by M.N. Venkatachaliah, not R.S. Sarkaria; in the Second ARC V. Ramachandran succeeded Veerappa Moily in 2009, not the reverse; and the Kurian Joseph Committee (2025) was set up by Tamil Nadu, not Kerala.

st.3: The DMK, founded in 1949, originally demanded Dravidanadu and formed the Tamil Nadu government in 1967 under M. Karunanidhi.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The Akali Dal's first president was Sarmukh Singh Jhabal, not Master Tara Singh; and the DMK formed the Tamil Nadu government in 1967 under C.N. Annadurai, not M. Karunanidhi.

st.1: Under full State funding the State bears all legitimate costs while private donations continue to be allowed.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Under full State funding private donations are banned, not allowed alongside; and the Indrajit Gupta Committee recommended partial State funding in kind, not full funding in cash.

st.2: It began as the single Etawah pilot project of Albert Mayer.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. The CDP began with 55 pilot community projects, the Etawah project (1948) being only a forerunner; and it was pioneered by S.K. Dey, later Union Minister of Community Development, not V.T. Krishnamachari.

st.4: Under Article 243Y, a separate Finance Commission must be set up to review the finances of Municipalities.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Fifth SFC recommended extra help to local bodies with low, not high, per capita income; and under Article 243Y the same State Finance Commission reviews the finances of Municipalities, with no separate commission.

st.2: The Panchayat Secretary presides over Gram Panchayat meetings.

x: Neither statement is correct. Gram Panchayat meetings are convened by the Panchayat Secretary on the Sarpanch's direction, not by the Sarpanch; and they are presided over by the Sarpanch, not the Panchayat Secretary.

st.1: It conducts elections to local bodies but not to co-operative societies.

x: All three statements are correct: the SEC conducts local-body polls but not co-operative polls; the Commissioner is appointed by the Governor for five years and removable only like a High Court Judge; and the residuary State's SEC was constituted on 30 January 2016.

st.2: A stagnant or declining population is one of the criteria for identifying a PVTG.

x: All three statements are correct: there are 75 PVTGs in 18 States and 1 UT; a stagnant or declining population is one of the criteria; and Andhra Pradesh has 12 PVTGs, including the Chenchu.

st.2: The National Sickle Cell Elimination Mission aims to eliminate the disease by 2030.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. PM-AJAY is run by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment for Scheduled Castes, not by Tribal Affairs for STs; and the Sickle Cell Elimination Mission aims at elimination by 2047, not 2030.

st.2: A dual rate under LERMS (1992) gave way to full capital-account convertibility from March 1993.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The rupee's rate is market-determined, not pegged to a basket; and LERMS's dual rate gave way in March 1993 to a unified market-determined rate, not full capital-account convertibility, which India still does not have.

st.3: In DBFO, the private partner designs, builds, finances and operates the project.

x: All three statements are correct: in BOOT the private player owns the asset during the concession and then transfers it; BOLT is Build-Own-Lease-Transfer; and in DBFO the private partner designs, builds, finances and operates the project.

st.2: DARPG functions under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions.

x: All three statements are correct: CPGRAMS was launched in 2007 by DARPG, which works under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, and it is accessible 24x7 through the web, an app and UMANG.

st.3: The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined in 2014.

x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The first lateral-entry Joint Secretaries joined in 2019, not 2014.

st.2: The 2007 policy treats NGOs as implementing agencies subordinate to government.
st.4: The focus of civil society has shifted from rights, advocacy and watchdog work to welfare delivery.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The 2007 policy was brought out by the Planning Commission, not NITI Aayog (set up in 2015); it treats NGOs as partners of government, not subordinates; and civil society's focus has shifted from welfare delivery to rights, advocacy and watchdog work, not the reverse.

st.3: Pecuniary jurisdiction is decided by the value of compensation claimed.
st.4: The e-Jagriti facility has been merged into e-Daakhil.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. An appeal from a State Commission to the National Commission lies within 30 days, not 45; pecuniary jurisdiction now depends on the value of consideration paid, not the compensation claimed; and e-Daakhil has been merged into e-Jagriti, not the reverse.

st.2: Phase 2 of the fisheries talks (overcapacity and overfishing) was concluded at MC14 in Yaounde.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct: India was the 123rd member to deposit its acceptance (July 2026), and the TFA and the Fisheries Subsidies Agreement are the only two new multilateral WTO agreements in 30 years. Phase 2 was not concluded at MC14 but deferred to the General Council in Geneva.

st.2: Telangana and Uttarakhand are placed in the narrowing-window phase.

x: All three statements are correct: Kerala and Tamil Nadu are in the ageing phase, Telangana and Uttarakhand in the narrowing-window phase, and Kerala's 60+ share is projected at 22.8% by 2036.

st.3: Under Section 7 of the Aadhaar Act, 2016, Aadhaar may be required for subsidies paid from the Consolidated Fund of India.

x: All three statements are correct: Puttaswamy (2017) made privacy a fundamental right under Article 21; the 2018 verdict upheld Section 7 and struck down Section 57 by 4:1; and Section 7 covers subsidies from the Consolidated Fund of India.

st.1: It covers all severely disabled persons aged 18-79 years with 80% or more disability, whether or not they are BPL.

x: Neither statement is correct. IGNDPS covers only BPL persons aged 18-79 with 80% or more disability, not all disabled persons; and it pays ₹300 a month, not ₹200.

st.1: Launched on 2 October 2019, it aims at a Functional Household Tap Connection to every rural household and to schools, anganwadis, GP buildings and health centres.

x: Statements 2 and 3 are correct. Jal Jeevan Mission was launched on 15 August 2019, not 2 October 2019; and States other than the Himalayan and NE States share its cost with the Centre 50:50, not 60:40.

st.1: Its forerunner, Rajiv Aarogyasri, was launched in April 2007 for families above the poverty line.
st.4: It covers 2,059 procedures.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Rajiv Aarogyasri (April 2007) was for BPL families, not APL families; the Rs 25 lakh cap does not apply to cancer, which has no limit; and the scheme now covers 3,257 procedures, not 2,059.

st.1: The MMR of Andhra Pradesh is 30, against 97 for India.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. India's MMR in SRS 2021-23 is 88, not 97, against 30 for Andhra Pradesh; and the IMR of Andhra Pradesh is 19 against 25 for India, not the reverse.

st.2: Primary education is not one of its components.

x: All three statements are correct: the Bare Necessities Index measured access at the State level, it excludes primary education, and it was built from the NSO's 69th and 76th rounds.

st.2: MSMEs account for about 48.58% of GDP and 31.1% of exports.
st.4: The Aspirational Blocks Programme (January 2023) covers 112 blocks.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. MSMEs account for about 31.1% of GDP and 48.58% of exports, not the reverse; VB-G RAM G raised guaranteed employment from 100 to 125 days, not 150; and the Aspirational Blocks Programme covers 500 blocks, 112 being the number of Aspirational Districts.

st.4: The Code on Social Security is the only one of the four Codes enacted in 2019.
st.1: Labour is in the Union List, and 29 Central laws were merged into four Codes.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Labour is in the Concurrent List, not the Union List; the national floor wage is fixed by the Central Government, not the States; and the Code on Wages, not the Social Security Code (2020), is the only Code enacted in 2019.

st.1: The 13th Finance Commission raised the States' share in the divisible pool to 30.5%.
st.4: The 14th Finance Commission used contribution to GDP as a criterion for the first time.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The 13th FC raised the States' share to 32% (30.5% was the 12th FC's); the 14th FC gave income distance a weight of 50% (47.5% was the 13th FC's fiscal capacity distance); and the 14th FC introduced forest cover, contribution to GDP being the 15th FC's new criterion.

st.3: Ashok Kumar Lahiri was a former Chief Economic Adviser before becoming Vice-Chairperson.

x: All three statements are correct: NITI's Vice-Chairperson and CEO are separate posts, Nidhi Chhibber served as interim CEO, and Ashok Kumar Lahiri is a former Chief Economic Adviser.

st.2: The 1978 demonetisation was carried out when Morarji Desai was Prime Minister.

x: All three statements are correct: the 1946 notes were demonetised by an ordinance, and the 1978 demonetisation came under Morarji Desai through the High Denomination Bank Notes (Demonetisation) Act.

st.1: Under the Finance Act, 2019 the regulation of housing finance companies moved from NHB to SEBI, while NHB keeps supervision and refinance.
st.3: After the IL&FS defaults of September 2018, its board was superseded by an order of the RBI.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The Finance Act, 2019 moved HFC regulation from NHB to the RBI, not SEBI; NHB was wholly owned by the RBI until the Centre took it over in 2019, not 2008; and the IL&FS board was superseded through an NCLT order, not by the RBI.

st.3: They have direct access to the RBI's LAF (repo) window.
st.1: They can issue cheques drawn on themselves, like banks.

x: None of the statements is correct. NBFCs cannot issue cheques drawn on themselves; their deposits are not covered by DICGC insurance; and they have no access to the RBI's LAF (repo) window.

st.1: The Annual Financial Statement is laid before Parliament under Article 112 of the Constitution.

x: All three statements are correct: the Annual Financial Statement is laid under Article 112, not the FRBM Act; the rolling fiscal targets have been suspended since 2021-22; and the MTEF Statement, added in 2012, is laid after the Budget.

st.1: The GST constitutional amendment did not need ratification by the State legislatures.

x: Neither statement is correct. The GST amendment had to be ratified by at least half the State legislatures; and VAT was levied under Entry 54 of the State List, not Entry 52.

st.1: Green Box support, such as farmer training and extension, is capped at the de minimis level.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Green Box support is permitted without limit, not capped at the de minimis level; and the Amber Box de minimis limit is 5% for developed and 10% for developing countries, not the reverse.

st.1: It was started by Acharya Vinoba Bhave at Paunar (Wardha) on 18 April 1951.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Bhoodan began at Pochampally on 18 April 1951, not at Paunar; and landowners were asked to donate one-sixth of their land, not one-fourth.

st.2: NABARD's SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was launched in 1992.

x: All three statements are correct: bank nationalisation and the Lead Bank Scheme both came in 1969, the SHG-Bank Linkage Programme was launched in 1992, and it is the world's largest microfinance programme.

st.4: The strategic reserve comprises 20 LMT wheat and 30 LMT rice.
st.1: Buffer norms are fixed by the CACP quarterly, as on 1 April, 1 July, 1 October and 1 January.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Buffer norms are fixed by the CCEA, not the CACP; stocks of 604.02 LMT on 1 April 2026 were nearly three times the 210.40 LMT norm, not five times; and the strategic reserve is 30 LMT wheat and 20 LMT rice, not the reverse.

st.2: In minority disinvestment the government sells a majority stake and gives up management control.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. In minority disinvestment the government keeps more than 51% and control, selling a majority with control being a strategic sale; and removing licences, quotas and controls without any sale of equity is deregulation, not privatisation, which transfers ownership or management.

st.1: Direct employment in the IT-BPM industry was about 85 lakh in FY2025.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. Direct IT-BPM employment was about 58 lakh in FY2025, not 85 lakh; and most IT-BPM jobs are organised, with contracts and social security.

st.2: The revenue lost with Hyderabad was mainly corporate taxes, stamp duties and commercial taxes, not agricultural land revenue.

x: All three statements are correct: the Hyderabad region gave nearly 50% of undivided AP's revenue, mainly corporate taxes, stamp duties and commercial taxes, and residual AP kept its agricultural base.

st.2: Interest receipts, dividends and fees are capital receipts.
st.4: Pensions are capital expenditure.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Interest receipts, dividends and fees are non-tax revenue, not capital receipts; market borrowings are capital receipts, not revenue receipts; and pensions are revenue expenditure, not capital expenditure.

st.2: SASCI loans are 50-year interest-free loans kept outside the 3% of GSDP fiscal-deficit cap.

x: All three statements are correct: Special Category Status was promised in Parliament for five years; SASCI loans are 50-year interest-free loans outside the 3% cap; and AP said it lost up to ₹38,000 crore when the 16th FC discontinued revenue deficit grants.

st.4: The revenue/capital distinction was ended.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Outcome Budget dates from 2005, not 2017-18; and it was the Plan/non-Plan distinction, not the revenue/capital distinction, that Budget 2017-18 ended.

st.2: Funds under the package are tied to approved EAPs, while SCS funds can be used for all schemes.

x: All three statements are correct: under SCS CSS funding is an automatic 90:10 grant while the package gives the equivalent only via EAP repayments; package funds are tied to approved EAPs; and industry gets only the weaker Section 94(1) incentives.

st.2: PKVY clusters are certified by the Bureau of Indian Standards (BIS).

x: Neither statement is correct. NMNF promotes natural farming with no external inputs, not organic farming; and PKVY organic clusters are certified under PGS-India, not by the BIS.

st.1: They were started in 2009 for farmers to sell directly to consumers.
st.4: About 1,290 Rythu Bazars are functioning.
st.3: Prices are fixed about 25% below wholesale prices.

x: None of the statements is correct. Rythu Bazars were started in 1999, not 2009; each is run by an Estate Officer of the Agricultural Marketing Department, not the District Collector; prices are fixed about 25% above wholesale and below local retail prices, not below wholesale; and about 129, not 1,290, are functioning.

st.2: It was concentrated mainly on the Krishna, Godavari and Pennar rivers.

x: All three statements are correct: Jalayagnam aimed to irrigate 1 crore acres and stabilise 21 lakh acres, it was concentrated on the Krishna, Godavari and Pennar, and residual AP counts 40 Jalayagnam projects.

st.2: The Indo-Israel Centre of Excellence for Vegetables and Flowers in Andhra Pradesh, set up under it, is at Kuppam.

x: All three statements are correct: MIDH subsumed the 2005-06 National Horticulture Mission, the Indo-Israel Centre of Excellence for Vegetables and Flowers is at Kuppam, and HMNEH is one of its sub-schemes.

st.3: The discovery of Eris triggered the change.

x: All three statements are correct: Pluto was reclassified at the IAU General Assembly in Prague in August 2006, it fails the test of clearing its orbit, and the discovery of Eris triggered the change.

st.2: Unequal lengths of day and night are caused by the changing distance between the Earth and the Sun.
st.1: Day and night are caused by the revolution of the Earth.

x: Neither statement is correct. Day and night are caused by the Earth's rotation, not its revolution; and unequal days and nights result from the tilt of the axis together with revolution, not from the changing Earth–Sun distance.

st.2: Cyclone Montha (October 2025) was steered north-northwest to the Tamil Nadu coast near Chennai.

x: Neither statement is correct. Tropical cyclones in the Northern Hemisphere spin anticlockwise, not clockwise; and Cyclone Montha was steered to the Kakinada coast of Andhra Pradesh, not the Tamil Nadu coast.

st.3: The India Meteorological Department lists about 340 geothermal sites.
st.1: Iceland's Haukadalur valley has the largest number of geysers, including Old Faithful.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Yellowstone in the USA, not Iceland's Haukadalur, has the most geysers and Old Faithful; the 340 geothermal sites are listed by the Geological Survey of India, not the IMD; and basaltic plateaus such as the Deccan weather into black (regur) soil, not red soil.

st.1: Climate and biological activity are passive factors of soil formation.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. Climate and biological activity are active, not passive, factors of soil formation; and the river silts behind AP soils are those of the Godavari, Krishna and Penna, the Mahanadi lying outside the State.

st.2: The Meseta lies in the Balkan Peninsula.
st.1: The Pamir plateau, the highest and largest, averages about 4,500 m.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The Tibetan plateau, not the Pamir, is the highest and largest; the Meseta lies in the Iberian, not the Balkan, Peninsula; and the Anatolian plateau lies between the Pontic and Taurus ranges, not the Zagros.

st.2: Carbon dioxide is the most abundant greenhouse gas and acts as a feedback.
st.1: Nitrous oxide is known as 'marsh gas'.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. Marsh gas is methane, not nitrous oxide; water vapour, not CO₂, is the most abundant greenhouse gas; and over 100 years methane's GWP is 28–36 and nitrous oxide's 265–298, not the reverse.

st.3: Uttar Pradesh shares international borders with Nepal and China.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. Nagaland borders only Myanmar, not Bangladesh; and Uttar Pradesh borders only Nepal, not China.

st.3: The transferred mandals now lie in Kakinada district.
st.1: Seven Warangal mandals were moved to Andhra Pradesh in 2014 to facilitate the Polavaram Irrigation Project.

x: Only statement 4 is correct. The seven mandals came from Khammam, not Warangal; Bhadrachalam town stayed in Telangana; and the mandals now lie in Polavaram district, not Kakinada.

st.2: The Eastern Ghats are younger and higher than the Western Ghats.

x: Statements 1 and 4 are correct. The Eastern Ghats are older and lower than the Western Ghats, not younger and higher; and in AP it is the Godavari and the Krishna, not the Penna, that split them into the Eastern Ranges and the Kadapa Ranges.

st.1: It is caused by the retreating north-east monsoon winds striking the Western Ghats.

x: Neither statement is correct. The west coast's heavy rain comes from the moist south-west monsoon winds off the Arabian Sea striking the Western Ghats, not the north-east monsoon; and it is orographic, not convectional.

st.3: Diviseema is the wedge of land between the two branches of the Krishna.

x: All three statements are correct: the Krishna rises near Mahabaleshwar and meets the sea at Hamsaladeevi, it splits at Puligadda about 64 km below Vijayawada, and Diviseema lies between its two branches.

st.1: The Veligonda project is named after Tanguturi Prakasam.

x: All three statements are correct: Puducherry's legislature rests on Article 239A (14th Amendment), Delhi's NCT status on Article 239AA (69th Amendment), and Puducherry is closest to a State, J&K having the least autonomy.

st.3: A name could be vetoed only by the Chief Justice of India.
st.4: The collegium is expressly mentioned in Article 124.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. The NJAC was to be chaired by the CJI, not the Law Minister; any two of its members, not the CJI alone, could veto a name; and the collegium is not mentioned in the Constitution.

st.4: As per Census 2011, Hindus were 80.5% of the population.
st.1: Census 2027 comes after a 6-year delay and uses only paper schedules.
st.3: As per Census 2011, Buddhists recorded the lowest decadal growth (5.4%) in 2001–11.

x: None of the statements is correct. Census 2027 is fully digital, not paper-based; geotagging is done during House-listing, not Population Enumeration; the lowest decadal growth in 2001–11 (5.4%) was of Jains, not Buddhists; and Hindus were 79.8% in 2011, 80.5% being the 2001 figure.

st.3: Russia ranks 3rd, ahead of India.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. SDRs are issued by the IMF, not the RBI; and the 3rd-ranked country is Switzerland, Russia having fallen behind India.

st.4: The MSF rate and Bank Rate now stand at 5.25%.

x: Statements 1 and 3 are correct. It was the first repo hike since February 2023, not May 2022; and the MSF rate and Bank Rate stand at 5.75%, 5.25% being the SDF rate.

st.1: India's milk production in 2024–25 was 247.87 MMT, with per capita availability of 459 g/day.

x: Statements 3 and 4 are correct. Per capita milk availability in 2024–25 was 485 g/day, not 459 g/day (the 2023–24 figure); and India ranks 4th, not 2nd, in world meat production.

st.1: Bollgard II, with three genes, was introduced in 2006.

x: Statements 2 and 4 are correct. Bollgard II carries two genes, not three; and the nodal cotton procurement agency is the Cotton Corporation of India, not the Cotton Board.

st.4: DPIIT is its Project Management Agency.
st.1: Its outlay is ₹33,660 crore for 2025–26 to 2030–31.
st.2: It envisages 100 plug-and-play industrial parks by 2047.

x: None of the statements is correct. BHAVYA's ₹33,660 crore covers 2026–27 to 2031–32, not 2025–26 to 2030–31; it envisages 100 parks by 2032, not 2047; the Centre bears up to 25%, not 50%, of external infrastructure cost; and NICDC, not DPIIT (which issues the guidelines), is the Project Management Agency.

st.4: India's trade deficit with China hit a record USD 99.21 billion in 2025.
st.2: UNCTAD put India's FDI inflow in 2025 at USD 47 billion, down 73%.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. The World Bank framework provides USD 8–10 billion a year for five years, not ten; UNCTAD's estimate of USD 47 billion was a rise of 73%, not a fall; and the record 2025 deficit with China was USD 116.12 billion, USD 99.21 billion being the 2024 figure.

st.3: In February 2026 the RBI lowered its current-year GDP projection from 7.4% to 7.3%.
st.1: In December 2025 the repo was cut by 25 bps to 5.25%, taking cumulative cuts since February 2025 to 150 bps.
st.2: The February 2025 cut was the RBI's first since February 2023.

x: None of the statements is correct. The December 2025 cut took cumulative cuts since February 2025 to 125 bps, not 150 bps; the February 2025 cut was the first since May 2020, not February 2023; in February 2026 the RBI raised its GDP projection from 7.3% to 7.4%, not lowered it; and the repo rate stayed at 5.25% in February 2026 rather than being cut to 5%.

st.1: Its logo is Gandhi's charkha and rural India was declared ODF by 2 October 2019.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The SBM logo is Gandhi's spectacles, not his charkha; and the three ODF Plus stages are Aspiring, Rising and Model, not Emerging.

st.2: Its Employer part gives incentives to employers for creating additional jobs.

x: All three statements are correct: the scheme is implemented through EPFO with ₹99,446 crore, its Employer part rewards employers for additional jobs (first-time entrants are covered by the employee part), and it targets 3.5 crore+ jobs during 1 August 2025 to 31 July 2027.

st.4: Punjab, Maharashtra, UP, Kerala and Rajasthan account for about 70% of rooftop installations.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. PM Surya Ghar is not financed by World Bank and AIIB loans; and the top rooftop States are Gujarat, Maharashtra, UP, Kerala and Rajasthan, Punjab's free power having cut its uptake.

st.2: In AP, children following the State syllabus must complete 5 years by 31 March.
st.1: Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act reserves 15% of Class 1 seats in private unaided schools for disadvantaged and EWS children.

x: None of the statements is correct. Section 12(1)(c) reserves 25%, not 15%, of Class 1 seats; for the State syllabus in AP the cut-off is 1 June, 31 March applying to IB/CBSE/ICSE; and the 2019 Amendment allows detention only in Classes 5 and 8, not in every class from Class 5.

st.2: It is lower than the record 2025–26 production of 376.56 million tonnes.

x: All three statements are correct: Shivraj Singh Chouhan announced a target of 373.93 million tonnes, which is lower than the record 376.56 million tonnes of 2025–26, and the Rabi target is 177.72 million tonnes.

st.1: It is prepared by NITI Aayog.
st.2: Andhra Pradesh ranked first, Goa second and Sikkim third.
st.3: Andhra Pradesh ranked first in per capita income among the States covered.

x: None of the statements is correct. The index is prepared by CNES, O.P. Jindal Global University, not NITI Aayog; Goa was first and Andhra Pradesh second, not the reverse; AP was 13th in per capita income, though 1st in socio-economic security; and the index uses 5 dimensions with 60 indicators, not 84.

st.3: In its term CBRNED, the letter 'D' stands for 'Drone'.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. PRAHAAR rests on seven pillars, not five; and in CBRNED the 'D' stands for 'Digital', not 'Drone'.

st.2: APCRDA hired a consultant to design a governance framework in line with the 73rd and 74th Amendments.

x: All three statements are correct: Amaravati's planned area is about 217 sq km assembled by land pooling, APCRDA's governance framework follows the 73rd and 74th Amendments, and CJI Surya Kant called mediation a pillar of justice.

st.1: All 175 Assembly constituencies were graded on 685 indicators.

x: All three statements are correct: all 175 constituencies were graded on 685 indicators, Guntur West alone was graded B–, and Vijayawada West topped with 93.

st.1: After MDUs were discontinued, doorstep delivery of rations continued only for senior citizens (65+) and persons with disabilities.

x: All three statements are correct: doorstep delivery continues for senior citizens and persons with disabilities, rice cards were issued for the first time to transgender persons, and AAY cards were identified for Chenchus, Yanadis and pensioned rural artists.

st.3: Cheaper fertilisers are supplied through Gromor centres.

x: All three statements are correct: Annadata Sukhibhava–PM Kisan gives ₹20,000 a year (State ₹14,000, Centre ₹6,000), it was launched on 2 August 2025 with ₹7,000 to each farmer, and cheaper fertilisers come through Gromor centres, Rythu Bazaars being for certified natural produce.

st.2: It targets a USD 4.2 trillion economy by 2047.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Swarna Andhra @2047 targets a USD 2.4 trillion economy, not USD 4.2 trillion; and it was not prepared with inputs from the Finance Commission.

st.3: The national average share above ₹5 lakh was 55.3%.

x: All three statements are correct: the data covered filers with income up to ₹50 lakh, Andhra Pradesh had the highest share above ₹5 lakh (62.1%), and the national average was 55.3%.

st.3: It was the first Budget prepared at North Block.
st.2: It was India's 5th Digital Budget.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. It was India's 6th Digital Budget, not the 5th; it was the first Budget prepared at Kartavya Bhavan, earlier Budgets having been prepared at North Block; and the Annual Financial Statement is laid under Article 112, not Article 110.

st.2: The National Quantum Mission, run by MeitY, was approved in April 2023 with ₹6,003.65 crore.

x: Only statement 3 is correct. IN-SPACe is headquartered at Ahmedabad, not Bengaluru; and the National Quantum Mission (April 2023, ₹6,003.65 crore) is run by the Department of Science and Technology, not MeitY.

st.2: MDL will invest about ₹15,000 crore for a capacity of 1.2 million gross tonnes a year.

x: All three statements are correct: the MDL–NSHIP-AP MoU was signed on 18 September 2026, MDL will invest about ₹15,000 crore for 1.2 million gross tonnes a year, and MDL is a Navratna PSU under the Ministry of Defence, headquartered at Mumbai.

st.3: It will make about 96 million chips a year at a cost of ₹2,387.81 crore.

x: All three statements are correct: the unit is by ASIP Technologies with APACT at Tarluvada, it is AP's first and South India's first OSAT unit under the ISM, and it will make about 96 million chips a year at ₹2,387.81 crore.

st.2: Maize is India's second food crop after rice.
st.1: India's first non-GMO high-expansion popcorn maize hybrids were released by Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan at Musunuru, Eluru, with ICAR-IIMR.

x: None of the statements is correct. The popcorn maize hybrids were released by Vice-President C.P. Radhakrishnan, not Shivraj Singh Chouhan; maize is India's third food crop after rice and wheat, not second; and Lam BG-II 2208 is a straight variety whose seed can be reused, not a hybrid.

st.4: Besides PSUs, it now also guards India's land borders.

x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The CISF is a CAPF under the Ministry of Home Affairs, not Defence; and besides PSUs it guards airports, metros, seaports and heritage monuments, not India's land borders.

st.1: They were held at Hangzhou, China, from 18 to 24 October 2026.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The 5th Asian Para Games were held at Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, not Hangzhou; and the first Asian Para Games were held at Guangzhou in 2010, not Incheon in 2014.

st.2: ASR district ranked first in India in Basic Infrastructure under NITI Aayog's Aspirational Districts Programme (March 2026).

x: All three statements are correct: ASR district was formed on 4 April 2022 with headquarters at Paderu, it ranked first in Basic Infrastructure under the Aspirational Districts Programme, and K. Dinesh Kumar is the first Collector of Polavaram district (HQ Rampachodavaram).

st.3: It is held under DAY-NRLM.

x: All three statements are correct: the National SARAS Mela-2026 was held at Vijayawada, the first time outside Delhi-NCR, organised by the Union Ministry of Rural Development, the AP Government and SERP, under DAY-NRLM.

st.2: The three inscriptions, dated 1554, are in Telugu, Tamil and Kannada.

x: All three statements are correct: the inscriptions were found by the ASI epigraphy team led by K. Munirathnam Reddy, the three 1554 records are in Telugu, Tamil and Kannada, and the main one records Sadasiva Raya's visit and the building of a Siva temple and mutt at Papavinasam.

st.1: There is a central bank at Kondapalli and six others.

x: Neither statement is correct. The central Craft Wood Bank is at Dowleswaram, not Kondapalli; and the National Mission on Handicrafts comes under the Ministry of Textiles, not Culture.

st.1: It was organised by the Indian Coast Guard to mark 150 years of Vande Mataram, written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

x: Only statement 2 is correct. The Cyclothon was organised by the CISF, not the Indian Coast Guard; and it covered about 6,500 km across 9 coastal States, not 11.

st.3: No major DRDO laboratory is headquartered in Andhra Pradesh.

x: All three statements are correct: DRDO was set up in 1958 under the Ministry of Defence, it led Mission Shakti, and no major DRDO laboratory is headquartered in Andhra Pradesh, though the State has test facilities and collaborations.

st.2: Garimella Balakrishna Prasad received the Padma Bhushan in 2026 posthumously.

x: Only statement 1 is correct. Garimella Balakrishna Prasad received the Padma Shri, not the Padma Bhushan, posthumously in 2026; and Boyi Bhimanna received the Padma Shri in 1973, the 2001 award being the Padma Bhushan.

st.1: ODOP is run by DPIIT with the States.

x: All three statements are correct: ODOP is run by DPIIT with the States, 99 AP products had been identified by July 2026, and four of the 10 State-level ODOP awards went to handloom products.

st.2: 71 warships were reviewed from INS Sumedha.

x: All three statements are correct: IFR 2026, the 3rd, was held at Visakhapatnam on 18 February 2026, 71 warships were reviewed from INS Sumedha, and its theme was 'United through Oceans'.
